issue.body:
## Request

Maintainer, 2026-11-02, quoted verbatim:

> 1. I agree. We can also move to an index-oriented file where we create nested directories and store by month (or week/day if needed) to not let the files stack up.
>
> 2. Let's go with your recommendation, but make sure we have an issue homed in a milestone in the backlog to work through this.

## Current state and immediate disposition

This is later work in **M6: Codebase renovation**, explicitly milestone-backed at the maintainer's request. It does not expand T39's current correction pass or become a release gate.

T39 #686 / audit #1406 has accepted Stage-D evidence at `96ef183aae39da587e5dc51d19d7c1fc9e850704`. Its menu-map journal contains 279 historical lines under 16 headings; two headings still describe closed work as pending. The immediate correction keeps that journal in place, marks its historical status and corrects the headings. Follow-up organization should make the live reference an index into dated material, with nested directories grouped by month and week/day subdivisions only where volume warrants them.

T39's accepted Q5 result identifies 33 reference documents / 2,770 lines with few incoming repository links (69 table rows, population 70). This measures links, not readership. The immediate correction keeps these documents and dates/labels records that could otherwise look current. Follow-up reviews each document's purpose and replacement before proposing retirement. No bulk deletion follows from a low link count. The accepted population includes 32 T39 edit-scope files and one historical plan (`plans/conflict-resolution/vita-style-conflict-resolution.md`); the latter remains a table-only ledger row in T39. Its later review belongs here, without expanding the current lane's edit scope.

Evidence: [journal question](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/issues/686#issuecomment-6582760931), [reference-document question](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/issues/686#issuecomment-6582762282), [accepted Stage-D packet](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/96ef183aae39da587e5dc51d19d7c1fc9e850704/docs/audits/2026_11_01-epic-m6-doctrine-reference). D-WORKFLOW-223 and D-WORKFLOW-224 record the dispositions; #346 coordinates the queue.

## Work to deliver

1. Introduce a compact index for the dated documentation, starting with the menu-map journal. Use nested year/month directories and only add week/day subdivisions when needed. Define where new entries go so neither one narrative file nor one flat directory grows indefinitely. Preserve original dates, content provenance, headings and links through an explicit old-to-new mapping.
2. Review the 33 accepted Q5 candidates individually. Record the document's purpose, current consumers or useful context, factual currency, any replacement and a disposition: retain as current, retain as historical, consolidate or retire. A document's low inbound count alone is insufficient evidence for retirement. Account separately for additions or changes since the accepted source hash.
3. Implement supported dispositions and update callers, indexes and links together. Keep dated evidence and applicable credits; do not turn this into an operating-system, legal-notice or source-code rewrite. Current T39 fixes stay owned by #686; record their completed status rather than repeat them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A retained disposition table covers exactly the 33 accepted Q5 candidates by path, with purpose/context, replacement evidence where applicable and an explicit outcome; a drift section accounts separately for changes after `96ef183aae39da587e5dc51d19d7c1fc9e850704`.
- [ ] The live menu reference links to a compact journal index and nested monthly storage; a recorded tree listing and index-link resolution check demonstrate that all retained journal entries are discoverable, with any week/day subdivision justified by the resulting directory contents.
- [ ] A migration manifest maps every moved journal heading or document to its new location, preserves dated provenance/content, and records the repaired incoming path, anchor and line citations; the retained link-check output has zero unresolved links introduced by this change.
- [ ] Each consolidation or retirement has a recorded replacement or evidence that its purpose has ended; the before/after diff and disposition table agree, with no document removed solely because of a low inbound count.
- [ ] The resulting index documents the placement rule for future entries, and a source readback shows current versus historical status and superseding links wherever retained documents could otherwise mislead a reader.
- [ ] The issue's milestone and the M6 later-work section point to each other; final source/record checks and the closing report identify the delivered commits and any separately tracked unresolved work.

Can this be done on the VM? No -- repository documents, immutable Git history, the disposition table and link-resolution output establish these documentation claims. No build, guest, physical-device or cloud action is part of this work.

Already written: existing issues, rules and reference pages cite the current paths and sometimes line numbers. The migration manifest and caller updates preserve those readers' routes; earlier audit evidence remains attributed to its original tree.

description: "Use when analyzing complex problems requiring multiple passes. Progressive refinement methodology for thorough analysis."
---

# Multi-Pass Iterative Analysis Pattern

**Purpose**: Structured methodology for analyzing collections of items (issues, PIs, files, patterns) for classification, prioritization, or reconciliation using explicit N-to-N cross-referencing.

**Core Principle**: When analyzing a collection, partial context leads to missed relationships. The multi-pass approach with explicit cross-referencing ensures completeness.

**When to Apply**:
- Potential improvement tracking
- Issue triage/pruning
- Milestone priority evaluation
- Pattern extraction for instruction files
- Documentation audit
- Any "review all X and decide Y" task

---

## Quick Reference

### The Seven Passes

| Pass | Name | Purpose | Output |
|------|------|---------|--------|
| 1 | **Inventory** | Enumerate all items in scope | Item list with metadata |
| 2 | **Clustering** | Group by source/theme/relationship | Cluster map |
| 3 | **Individual Assessment** | Evaluate each item against criteria | Per-item analysis |
| 4 | **Cross-Reference** | Compare each item vs ALL others | Relationship matrix |
| 5 | **Classification** | Assign category/priority/status | Classification decisions |
| 6 | **Reconciliation** | Resolve conflicts/overlaps | Action plan |
| 7 | **Action** | Execute decisions with tracking | Completed actions |

### Rigor Levels

| Level | Use Case | Passes Used | Cross-Reference Scope |
|-------|----------|-------------|----------------------|
| **Quick Scan** | Spot-check, minor changes | 1, 3, 5 | Obvious relationships only |
| **Standard** | Regular gardening, re-triage | 1-5, 7 | Within-cluster comparison |
| **Comprehensive** | First analysis, milestone boundaries | All 7 | N-to-N (ALL items) |

**Default Selection**:
- First analysis of a scope: **Comprehensive**
- Re-analysis after prior pass: **Standard**
- Quick hygiene check: **Quick Scan**

---

## Core Principles

### N-to-N Cross-Referencing

**The differentiator**: Every item compared against every other item at least once.

**Why this matters**:
- Partial comparison misses non-obvious relationships
- Items may overlap with "unrelated" clusters
- Hidden dependencies only visible through comprehensive review

**Implementation**:
```
For item A in collection:
  For item B in collection (B ≠ A):
    Assess: Does A relate to B? (overlap, dependency, conflict)
    Record: Relationship type and evidence
```

**Scaling**: For large collections (50+ items), batch by cluster then cross-reference across clusters.

### Cluster-First Analysis

**Before individual analysis, identify clusters**:

1. Scan all item titles/summaries
2. Group by source (same Epic, same domain, same type)
3. Label clusters with descriptive names
4. Process clusters together to identify within-cluster relationships

**Example Clusters**:
- Cluster A: "Learning Loop Documentation" (#1, #2, #3, #4)
- Cluster B: "Epic Documentation Gaps" (#5, #6, #7)
- Cluster C: "Research Spikes" (#8, #9, #10)

**Why cluster first**:
- Identifies obvious relationships early
- Reduces cognitive load during individual assessment
- Enables batch decisions for homogeneous clusters

### Running Notes (Context Preservation)

**MANDATORY**: Create tracking file before starting.

**Required Contents**:
1. **Status tracker**: Phase/pass progress, counts, completion status
2. **Item-by-item table**: ID, cluster, analysis completed, classification
3. **Evidence annotations**: Rationale for each decision
4. **Cross-reference notes**: Relationships discovered

**Purpose**: Enable recovery after context loss (auto-compact, session break).

**Template**:
```markdown
# Analysis Tracking: [SCOPE] - [DATE]

## Progress
- Pass 1 (Inventory): ✅ Complete (N items)
- Pass 2 (Clustering): ✅ Complete (X clusters)
- Pass 3 (Individual): 🔄 In Progress (Y/N complete)
- Pass 4 (Cross-Reference): ⏳ Pending
...

## Item Analysis Table
| ID | Cluster | Pass 3 | Pass 4 | Classification | Evidence |
|----|---------|--------|--------|----------------|----------|
| #1 | A | ✅ | ✅ | VALID | No overlaps found |
| #2 | A | ✅ | 🔄 | - | Checking vs #5 |
...

## Relationships Discovered
- #1 and #5: Partial overlap (~30%), reconciliation needed
- #3 blocks #7: Dependency discovered
...
```

---

## Pass Descriptions

### Pass 1: Inventory

**Goal**: Complete enumeration of all items in scope with metadata.

**Actions**:
1. Query/list all items in scope
2. Capture: ID, title, created date, last modified, current status
3. Verify count matches expectations
4. Record in tracking file

**Output**: Item list with metadata

**Verification**: "I expect N items. I have retrieved N items."

### Pass 2: Clustering

**Goal**: Group items by source/theme before individual analysis.

**Actions**:
1. Scan all titles for patterns
2. Identify grouping criteria (source Epic, domain, type, date range)
3. Assign each item to exactly one cluster
4. Label clusters descriptively
5. Record cluster map in tracking file

**Output**: Cluster map (Cluster → Items)

**Cluster Naming**: Use descriptive names, not just letters.
- Good: "Learning Loop Documentation Layer Gap"
- Bad: "Cluster A"

### Pass 3: Individual Assessment

**Goal**: Evaluate each item against defined criteria.

**Actions**:
1. Read full item content (body, comments, history)
2. Apply assessment criteria (depends on analysis type)
3. Note initial classification hypothesis
4. Flag items needing cross-reference attention
5. Record analysis in tracking file

**Output**: Per-item analysis notes

**Assessment Criteria Examples**:
- Triage: Staleness indicators, blocker status, scope clarity
- Prioritization: Dependency unlocking, quality improvement, time to value
- PI Gardening: Corrective vs exploratory, confidence level, staleness

### Pass 4: Cross-Reference

**Goal**: Compare each item against all others to find relationships.

**Actions**:
1. For each item, compare against all others in scope
2. Identify: Overlaps, dependencies, conflicts, supersession
3. Record relationship type and evidence
4. Flag items needing reconciliation
5. Update tracking file with relationships

**Output**: Relationship discoveries

**Relationship Types**:
- **Overlap**: Partial scope intersection (requires reconciliation)
- **Dependency**: A blocks B or A enables B
- **Supersession**: Newer item replaces older item's scope
- **Conflict**: Mutually exclusive approaches
- **None**: Independent items

**Comprehensive vs Standard**:
- Comprehensive: Compare ALL items vs ALL items
- Standard: Compare within clusters + spot-check across clusters

### Pass 5: Classification

**Goal**: Assign final category/priority/status to each item.

**Actions**:
1. Review Pass 3 (individual) and Pass 4 (cross-reference) findings
2. Apply classification criteria
3. Assign category with evidence
4. Update tracking file

**Output**: Classification decisions with evidence

**Evidence Annotation Format**:
```
VALID - [STATUS] (N-pass verified YYYY-MM-DD: [evidence summary])
```

### Pass 6: Reconciliation

**Goal**: Create action plan for conflicts, overlaps, dependencies.

**Actions**:
1. For each flagged relationship, determine resolution
2. Apply resolution principles (recency bias, scope clarity, etc.)
3. Create reconciliation plan
4. Document in tracking file

**Output**: Reconciliation action plan

**Resolution Principles**:
- **Recency Bias**: Favor newer items when scope overlaps
- **Consolidation**: Merge unique details into primary item
- **Dependency Ordering**: Ensure blockers resolved before dependents

### Pass 7: Action

**Goal**: Execute decisions with tracking and verification.

**Actions**:
1. Present findings for approval (interactive)
2. Execute approved actions immediately (not batched)
3. Record actions taken
4. Verify completion

**Output**: Completed actions with evidence

**Interactive Workflow**:
1. Present summary (counts by category)
2. Walk through each category
3. Get approval from the user
4. Execute immediately
5. Confirm completion
6. Move to next category

---

## Application Examples

### Potential Improvement Tracking

**Inventory**: List all potential improvement notes with metadata (created, modified, confidence)
**Clustering**: Group by domain, confidence level, or source task
**Assessment Criteria**: Corrective vs exploratory, staleness, duplicate detection
**Classification**: KEEP, ARCHIVE, MERGE, PROMOTE_TO_INSTRUCTION
**Action**: Update index, archive stale items, merge duplicates

### Issue Triage

**Inventory**: Query project board for target column
**Clustering**: Group by Epic, domain, type
**Assessment Criteria**: Staleness indicators, blocker status, scope clarity
**Classification**: VALID, STALE, SUPERSEDED, DUPLICATE, PREMATURE
**Action**: Close, move, or keep with updated status

### Milestone Priority Evaluation

**Inventory**: List all issues in milestone
**Clustering**: Group by dependency chain, domain
**Assessment Criteria**: Dependency unlocking, quality improvement, time to value
**Classification**: Priority order with rationale
**Action**: Update milestone body, create blocking relationships

---

## Anti-Patterns

### Skip Cross-Reference Pass

**Problem**: "I'll just assess each item individually"
**Risk**: Missed relationships, duplicate work, incorrect classifications
**Fix**: Always include Pass 4, adjust rigor level for scope

### No Running Notes

**Problem**: "I'll remember where I was"
**Risk**: Context loss makes recovery impossible
**Fix**: Create tracking file BEFORE starting, update in real-time

### Batch Actions at End

**Problem**: "I'll execute all actions after analysis complete"
**Risk**: Decision fatigue, context drift, missed approvals
**Fix**: Execute actions immediately after each category approval

### Skip Clustering

**Problem**: "I'll just process items in order"
**Risk**: Miss within-cluster relationships, inefficient processing
**Fix**: Always cluster first, even if clusters seem obvious

---

## Integration with Other Patterns

### Retrospective Depth Selection

Multi-pass analysis can trigger retrospectives:
- Analysis reveals systemic issues → L3 retrospective
- Pattern emerges across items → L2 pattern extraction
- Routine gardening → L1 work log entry

### Issue Commencement/Closure

Multi-pass analysis tasks follow standard commencement/closure:
- Commence: Status transitions, project status update
- Closure: Checklist, learning loop, cross-issue updates

### Potential Improvements

Multi-pass analysis may create potential improvement entries:
- Recurring pattern discovered → Track as potential improvement
- Process gap identified → Create potential improvement note

### Issue Creation from Findings

When the analysis surfaces follow-up work that should become a GitHub issue, classify by evidence shape per [`issue_creation.instructions.md` § Investigation-Sourced Findings](../github_integration/issue_creation.instructions.md). Default to **Spike** unless the analysis confirms both the problem and the fix path. A confirmed symptom with an unconfirmed cause is a Spike, not a Task.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Solution |
|---------|-------|----------|
| Missing relationships | Skipped cross-reference pass | Run Pass 4 comprehensively |
| Context loss during analysis | No tracking file | Create tracking file, resume from last recorded position |
| Inconsistent classifications | No evidence annotation | Re-run with explicit evidence recording |
| Scope creep during analysis | No inventory verification | Verify item count matches expectations |
| Decision paralysis | Too many items at once | Batch by cluster, process one cluster at a time |

---

## Related Instructions

- **Milestone Governance**: [`milestone_chain_authority.instructions.md`](../project_management/milestone_chain_authority.instructions.md) and [`phase_transition.instructions.md`](../project_management/phase_transition.instructions.md)
- **Potential Improvements**: Tracked via PI process (see [pi_tracking.instructions.md](../project_management/pi_tracking.instructions.md))

---

**Success Criteria**: Analysis produces complete, consistent classifications with evidence trail that survives context loss and enables audit.

**Confidence Check**:
1. Did I enumerate ALL items in scope?
2. Did I compare each item against ALL others (appropriate to rigor level)?
3. Can I point to evidence for each classification?
4. Can someone resume from my tracking file after context loss?

Maintainer, 2026-09-28, while chain 89 was being prepared: *"When this is all done, we should do a retro on everything that was identified in this comprehensive adversarial review process. We should figure out if there are updates we can make to our own instruction files by running this through our recursive learning abstraction process. To understand the meta learnings around this, if you need an example of how I'm doing this elsewhere, I can share one."*

**Scope of the review it looks back on:** the audit of the feature drop (#307, 78 items; #308, 297 sweep rows), the eight fix streams and their follow-ups (#309), the milestone-tier audit of the whole fix round with its two-pass second opinion (#313, 34 items; `docs/audits/2026_09_28-milestone-audit-of-the-fix-round/`), the wordlist work (#312), step 0 of the candidate, and the integrator's own slips of the day (the friction log, blindspots 66-68).

**What exists today:** `learning-capture.md` (a learning becomes a rule, a tool or a work-log entry; § 3 makes a procedure executable), `mini-retro` and `futro` (the ceremonies; `tools/ceremony-check`), `working-principles.md`'s enforcement ladder (written -> routed -> evidenced -> audited -> self-examining), `docs/blindspot-register.md` (each entry from 52 names its guard). The maintainer's own process elsewhere is the model to hold this against; its example is to be shared.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The maintainer's example of the recursive learning abstraction process is linked or pasted here (their offer above), and the retro names which of its steps this repository's `learning-capture.md` and the ceremonies already carry and which they do not.
- [ ] `docs/retros/<date>-adversarial-review-round.md` exists and `tools/ceremony-check` reads it as the retro (its output pasted here), covering: what the two seats found that the streams had not, what the blind pass found that the orchestrator had dropped (G2-B-05), what the refutation pass corrected (R-01..R-05), what the integrator got wrong the same day (the friction log's entries and their guards), and what the round cost in time to play and in build rounds.
- [ ] Every learning in the retro has one of three outcomes, named with its artifact: an instruction-file change (the commit), a tool or guard (the tool, with the constructed failure it was seen to catch), or a stated reason it does not generalize.
- [ ] `tools/rules-check` and `tools/register-check` are clean after the instruction-file changes, and each changed rule's front matter still says when it loads.
- [ ] The register carries a row for each decision the retro makes (cited by ID here), and `docs/blindspot-register.md` an entry for each new shape, with its guard.
- [ ] The next audit's brief (the `code-auditor` skill) carries what this retro says about packets, verdict carriage and the second-opinion passes, in the skill's own text, so the next run starts from it.

Runs after the candidate call on #236 (the retro looks back on a finished thing).
